target: route "hk-doubling" (hkd): the Holt-Klee ceiling h*_HK, the sink lift, the generalised blow-up readout, (T*), and the one-player +1 gadget

findings.result_name: hkd:one-plus-one (and the closing paragraph of the route's LaTeX)
findings.defect: The claim "These are the first unbounded lower bounds in the last three rows" is false for the h*_1 row, and the route's bound h*_1(m) >= m+6 is dominated there by a result already proved in frontier.tex; neither cor:stack-family nor prop:hstar-one-eight is cited anywhere in the route's output.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.7042 cor:stack-family proves, for EVERY k, a one-player stopping SSG with 7k Max vertices whose all-switches run has length 12k, i.e. h*_1(7k) >= 12k -- unbounded, slope 12/7 (nondegeneracy is needed only for the LP/HK transfer, and h*_1 is defined with ties allowed, cor:hstar-one). frontier.tex l.7126 prop:hstar-one-eight restates it: "cor:stack-family adds h*_1(7k) >= 12k for every k". cor:stack-family also proves h*_1(m1+m2+1) >= h*_1(m1)+h*_1(m2), which with h*_1(1)=1 already gives h*_1(m+2) >= h*_1(m)+1. So hkd:one-plus-one is a real but small improvement (+1 per dimension in place of +1 per two dimensions), not a first unbounded bound; and 12*floor(m/7) beats m+6 from m=14 on (m=14: 24 vs 20). The claim IS correct for the h*_HK and h*_LP rows (there the paper has only the isolated values h*_HK(14)>=h*_LP(14)>=24 and h*_LP(8)>=13).

findings.result_name: rem:hkd-found ("How they were found") in the paste-ready LaTeX
findings.defect: The remark attributes to s_7 (the height-20 orientation of hkd:records) the provenance and the structure of the height-17 orientation; as written it is a false statement about s_7 and contradicts hkd:doubling(c), which derives s_7 from the blow-up B_phi(s^(5),7).
findings.evidence: I computed all fourteen facets of the printed s_7: heights 8,9,9,9,9,10,10,10,10,10,11,11,11,12 with pairwise distinct sinks -- there is NO facet pair of height 13 with a common sink (f7.py). The object whose two direction-6 facets are Holt-Klee 6-cubes of height 13 with the common sink 0, whose readout is phi = 1_{0,3} of weight two (the only v<64 with bit 6 set in the outmap are 0 and 3), whose walk begins 68,3,93,57 = (4,1)->(3,0)->(29,1)->(57,0) and for which 17 = 3+13+1, is the height-17 orientation (f17.py, facets.py). The remark's own arithmetic "17=3+13+1" gives it away.

findings.result_name: the four-ceilings table in the route's LaTeX
findings.defect: The replacement table lists h*_LP(5) >= 9 and h*_1(5) >= 9, reverting a proved entry of frontier.tex; presented as "The four ceilings now read", it misstates the state of knowledge.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.7101 prop:hstar-one-five proves h*_1(5) >= 10 and h*_LP(5) >= 10 (a 346-vertex nondegenerate one-player game, run of length 10 from 01010) and says explicitly that it improves "the entries >=9 of rem:four-ceilings"; the table at l.6800 already reads >=10. (The value >=9 appears in the round-16 briefing, not in the paper.)

findings.defect: The statement "B_phi(s,z) has height 2h+2" asserts equality; the argument establishes only >= (it exhibits one walk), and the equality is false when h(u) is not maximal.
findings.evidence: exact_b.py / exact_b2.py: over all 728 acyclic USOs of the 3-cube, every u with h(u)>=1, both alternation phases and every readout free off the walk (386560 blow-ups), 185808 have height > 2h(u)+2 (e.g. seed (0,1,2,3,4,5,7,6), u=1, h=1, height 5 instead of 4; largest observed 9), while 0 have height < 2h+2. All violations have h(u) not maximal; with h(u) maximal there were 0 violations at m=3 and 0 over the 2048 alternating readouts on the m=4 seed of hkd:doubling(b). hkd:doubling(b),(c) both take u of maximal height, so no downstream number is affected.

findings.result_name: rem:hkd-rem-one-plus-one (the size bound N <= 717 at m = 11)
findings.defect: The vertex count omits the gadgets that realise the five rows (y,1): p = (1-eps)e_j, each of which is not a unit vector and therefore costs D_0 >= 1 fresh average vertices by lem:dyadic-row.
findings.evidence: 717 = 564 + 140 + 11 + 2, where 564 = 12 x 47 is the twelve original rows of the m=6 normal form (47 nonzero entries in all, denominator 2^12) and 140 = 20+28+29+32+31 is the five theta rows; the five (y,1) rows contribute nothing to that sum. lem:dyadic-row (frontier.tex l.994) charges ell*d average vertices per row and makes the gadget empty only "when the row is a unit vector", which (1-eps)e_j is not.

findings.defect: The theorem's nondegenerate variant needs a threshold theta of larger denominator than the 2^{2a+2} the proof bounds, and the proof asserts the avoidance without saying so.
findings.evidence: theta must avoid the 2^m numbers (1-eps)val_sigma(x_j), each a rational of denominator dividing 2^{D_0} times an integer <= 2^a (lem:denominator-sharp, l.1107); an open interval of length >= 2^{-2a-1} contains more than 2^m multiples of 2^{-K} only once K > 2a+m+1. The proof says only "theta ranges over an interval, so it may be chosen to avoid the finitely many numbers", so the remark's "the proof gives only D <= 2a+2 per step" is the bound for the degenerate version. (In my own five iterations the thresholds needed denominators 2^18 to 2^28 with a = O(m^2 D), so nothing breaks in practice.)

findings.defect: L(s) is literally the lem:hstar-super block product with the 1-cube as second block, z = 1 and the 1-cube's sink at 1; and h*(m+1) >= h*(m)+1 already follows from lem:hstar-super with l = 1. Only the Holt-Klee half of the theorem is new. The route says as much in its rem:hkd-rem-plus-one(2), so this is attribution, not a defect.
findings.evidence: Unwinding lem:hstar-super (frontier.tex l.5334) with l=1, s_2(0)={0}, s_2(1)=empty and z=1 gives exactly the new coordinate out at (o,0) and in at (v,0) for v != o, i.e. phi = 1_{o}. rem:four-ceilings (l.6800) already records that this product on the prop:hkfive witness is Holt-Klee of heights 12 and 13; my lift.py reproduces 12, 13, 14 at m=6,7,8.

findings.defect: The pool-dependent counts (85671 Holt-Klee 5-cube orientations from the facet search, 6274 / 188 / 3; 502 and 5685 6-cube orientations of height 13 and >=10; 1848 5-cube orientations of height 10 or 11; the 96 height-20 7-cube orientations) are not reproducible from the statements -- they are properties of the route's private search pools. They are labelled measured/scoped, which is honest, but "the doubling does not iterate on this material" is a statement about that material only.
findings.evidence: Everything in (d),(e) that the statement defines DID reproduce exactly: my own C census of the 4-cube (5541744 USOs, 4792176 acyclic, height histogram with 384 of height 7 -- all matching prop:auso-census) gives 785 Holt-Klee classes of height 5 or 6 (729 + 56, the 56 matching cor:blowup-parity), exactly 506 admitting some z = o^u (u != o) with (T), exactly 4 with h(u) = 6, and exactly 36 Holt-Klee blow-ups of height 14 over those four across all 4 x 2^16 readouts (census4.c, d_check.py, d36.py). A (T*) scan over the 36 at threshold h(u) >= 1 -- stronger than the claimed >= 9 -- found none (tsc, scan36_all.log), as did the same scan on s_7 at h(u) >= 14.

findings.result_name: hkd:records, hkd:facet, hkd:readout(a),(c), hkd:tstar, hkd:doubling(a),(b),(c), hkd:one-plus-one, hkd:crosstab
findings.defect: No defect: every computational claim I could rebuild from the statement reproduced, in two independent implementations.
findings.evidence: s_6 (m=6) and s_7 (m=7) as printed in the LaTeX are USOs, acyclic, Holt-Klee on every face, of BA heights 14 and 20, sink 13, maximal starts {21,29,53,61} and {45,47,109,111}, walks exactly as printed (wit.py, and again in C after I fixed my own verts[64] overflow); the route's files hkd_hk6_h14.txt and hkd_hk7_h20.txt equal the printed outmaps. The height-17 example checks out too. Rebuilding B_phi from thm:blowup's table with phi in place of the parity gives, from the m=4 seed with z=13 and support {1,8,9,10,12}, s_6 byte for byte, and from the m=5 seed with z=7 and the printed support, s_7 byte for byte (blow.py, blow5.py); the pure parity readout on that seed has height 14 but is NOT Holt-Klee, and parity flipped at the other maximal vertex 5 is, exactly as claimed (parity.py). hkd:doubling(a): my own complete scan of 728 x 8 x 256 = 1490944 configurations gives the height histogram ...,8:88704, 9:6912, 10:2304 with 0 Holt-Klee at height >= 9 and a Holt-Klee example at height 8 (scan3.py). hkd:facet reproves cleanly (I redid the Szabo-Welzl case analysis by hand) and 6000 admissible triples are USOs / 168 accidental USOs all satisfy the component condition / the BA step formula holds (facetchk.py). lem:stack re-verified from scratch: 24 of 192 fail, all acyclic-non-HK, pattern exactly as stated; 16 of 144, pattern exactly as stated (stackchk.py, stack24.py). hkd:tstar: the beta=0 facet of B_phi(s,z) IS D(s,z) for every phi (verified on 50 random (z,phi)), which proves it; the strictness witness reproduces exactly -- the 5-cube seed is Holt-Klee of height 8, h(28)=8, z = 9^28 = 21, all 80 2-faces satisfy (T), and D(s,21) fails Holt-Klee on the 4-face {x0,x3,x4,x5} at the origin with flow 3 < 4 (tstar.py). hkd:one-plus-one: I rebuilt the m=6 game of prop:oneplayer-runs from its printed normal form (run 25,14,33,6,37,46,45,44,16,56,24,28,12 of length 12, 0 tied incidences over all 64 strategies, Holt-Klee AUSO of height 12) and then applied the gadget five times with MY OWN eps = 2^-8 and my own thresholds 245529/2^18, 3913119/2^22, 7795667/2^23, 242663/2^18, 247516261/2^28: run lengths 13,14,15,16,17 at m=7..11, every row leaking (stopping), 0 tied incidences over all 2^m strategies at every stage, improvement orientations acyclic USOs of height equal to the run length, Holt-Klee at m=7,8, and the runs extend exactly as the route reports (...,12,76,204,460,972,1996) (g6.py, iterate.py, nff.py). L(s_6) and L(s_7) are Holt-Klee AUSOs of heights 15 and 21 (tsc). hkd:crosstab: my own scoped pool (3000 pairs from the 3840-element orbit, 43342 admissible readouts) reproduces the qualitative claims -- heights to 19, every orientation of height >= 16 cyclic, every acyclic one of height 14 or 15 non-Holt-Klee, Holt-Klee stopping at 13 -- and all twelve facets of s_6 have heights 6,7,8 (cross.py, facets.py). No standing error was found: no val_sigma by greedy iteration, no dict-literal row collapse, no sink-index collision, no pair test in place of the own-successor test, no target-equivalent oracle, no polynomial-class claim.

verdict: The mathematics reproduces. Every computational claim that is determined by a statement rather than by the route's private search pools I rebuilt independently in exact arithmetic with two engines, and all of it checked: h*_HK(6) >= 14 and h*_HK(7) >= 20 are real (the printed outmaps s_6 and s_7 are acyclic unique sink orientations, Holt-Klee on every face, of BA heights 14 and 20, and both are recovered byte for byte from the stated seed, translation and readout); the exhaustive 3-cube scan (1490944 configurations, best Holt-Klee height 8), the 4-cube census numbers (785 / 506 / 4 / 36), lem:stack (24 of 192, 16 of 144), the (T*) strictness witness and the (T*) scan over the 36 all come out exactly as claimed. hkd:facet, hkd:plus-one, hkd:readout(a),(c) and hkd:tstar are correctly proved -- I reconstructed each argument, and hkd:tstar has the one-line form \"D(s,z) is the beta=0 facet of B_phi(s,z), for every phi\", which I verified. hkd:one-plus-one is correct and I reproduced it end to end with my own epsilon and my own thresholds, getting nondegenerate stopping one-player games at m=7..11 with runs of length 13..17. Two claims do not survive. (1) The headline and the closing paragraph assert \"the first unbounded lower bounds in three of the four rows\"; this is false for the h*_1 row, where cor:stack-family (frontier.tex l.7042) already proves h*_1(7k) >= 12k for every k, with the better slope 12/7, and already gives +1 per two dimensions -- the route's theorem is a genuine but small sharpening (+1 per one dimension) that should be stated against cor:stack-family, which it never cites. (2) rem:hkd-found describes s_7 as found by the facet search with two height-13 facets sharing a sink; s_7's fourteen facets have heights 8 to 12 with distinct sinks, and the description belongs to the height-17 orientation -- as written the remark contradicts hkd:doubling(c). Four minor repairs: the replacement table reverts h*_1(5) and h*_LP(5) from the paper's proved >= 10 (prop:hstar-one-five) to >= 9; hkd:readout(b) claims height exactly 2h+2, which is false off maximal u (185808 counterexamples at m=3) though only >= is used; the N <= 717 count omits the five (y,1) gadgets; and the nondegeneracy clause needs a threshold denominator larger than the 2^{2a+2} the proof bounds. None of these touches the two records or the +1 laws, so the route's mathematical content stands after the repairs; sound is marked false only because of the two false claims above.
